clue.text: Time limit is reason you can't phone?

definitions.meaning: the time by which something must be done
read whimsically, a ... on the telephone stops you calling

explanation.surface: Someone explains that the cut-off point is why no call can be made.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadline is the cut-off moment for a task; a telephone line that has gone dead stops any call.

clue.text: Heads of dodgy enterprise exploit loss

indicators.note: heads of asks for the first letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: a feat is an exploit or achievement

explanation.surface: The bosses of a shady business take advantage of a financial loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploit' looks like a verb; it is the noun, a feat.
explanation.definitionFit: A defeat is a loss in a contest or battle.

clue.text: Man wants a vote on principle

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so these come first

parts.note: X is the mark made on a ballot paper
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A man insists on having a vote on a matter of principle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is not a person but the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a self-evident truth or basic principle accepted without proof.

clue.text: A £50 rate, working on the side

indicators.note: working means being worked over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the pound sign and also the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone charges a fixed fifty-pound fee for a job done as a sideline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges A, LL and RATE. 'on the side' suggests moonlighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral means relating to or situated at the side of something.

clue.text: Unattractive and plain, I go into salon finally for makeover

indicators.note: finally asks for the last letter of salon
a makeover remodels something, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plain person goes into a beauty salon for a makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives the opening N from 'salon'; 'for makeover' rearranges the rest into OOILPAINTING.
explanation.definitionFit: No oil painting is a British idiom for someone who is not good-looking.

clue.text: Examiner is more irritable without one

indicators.note: without tells us a piece is dropped from the comparative adjective

parts.note: testier means more irritable
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An exam invigilator is grumpier than usual, apparently because something is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without one' takes the I (one) out of TESTIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tester is a person who checks or inspects something, so an examiner.

clue.text: Isolated area in French grotto containing lake

parts.note: en is French for in

indicators.note: containing means the cave holds the lake inside it

parts.note: a grotto is a cave

explanation.surface: A remote spot inside a French grotto that has a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' puts L inside CAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclave is a territory or group cut off and surrounded by another.

clue.text: On retirement, I blast head for unpunctuality

indicators.note: retirement means going back, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: drat and blast are both mild curses
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A retired person cursing their own head for always being late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On retirement' turns I DRAT into TARDI; 'head' is the headland, NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tardiness is lateness, being slow to arrive.

clue.text: At the end, demote member in rank?

definitions.text: At the end, demote member in rank?

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: rate means a rank or class, as in a first-rate ship

indicators.note: at the end asks for the final letter of demote

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A query about finally demoting someone who belongs to the ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the end' picks E from 'demote', so that word serves twice; the whole clue is also the definition, with 'in' showing what goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To relegate is to move down to a lower rank, sending a member to the bottom.

clue.text: Pirate gets a bit of a shock, finding gun

parts.note: Captain Flint is the pirate in Stevenson's Treasure Island
a shock of hair is a thick mass, and a lock is a small piece of it

explanation.surface: A pirate gets a mild fright and then discovers a firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' looks like a fright, but here it is a shock of hair, of which a lock is a bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A flintlock is an old musket or pistol fired by a flint striking steel.

clue.text: Fool around in class, needing slap to restore peace?

indicators.note: in puts the reversed fool inside the class

parts.note: kind means class or sort

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an ass is a fool
slap is British theatrical slang for make-up

explanation.surface: A pupil messes about in class and needs a smack to bring calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' gives SSA. 'Slap' reads as a smack but is British theatrical slang for cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: To kiss and make up is to be reconciled after a quarrel, ending hostilities.

clue.text: Primarily Christmas air, "Noel" regularly featured?

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letter of the word that follows
regularly asks for every other letter of the two words air and Noel taken together

explanation.surface: A seasonal song in which the word Noel keeps cropping up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes alternate letters of AIRNOEL, giving AROL after the C. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A carol is a Christmas song, and many carols repeat the cry of Noel.

clue.text: Not all respect a large naval officer

indicators.note: not all means the word for respect loses its final letter

parts.note: to admire is to respect
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Someone does not fully respect a big man in the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not all' cuts the final letter, leaving ADMIR.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is the most senior rank of commissioned officer in a navy.

clue.text: Fighting half-heartedly, being merciful

indicators.note: the heart of the boxing word is a doubled letter, and half of that pair goes

parts.note: sparring is practice fighting, as in boxing

explanation.surface: A boxer who fights without real effort may be showing mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of SPARRING is RR; 'half-heartedly' removes one R.
explanation.definitionFit: To spare someone is to show them mercy, so sparing means being lenient or merciful.

clue.text: When out, English batsman feels humiliation

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An English cricketer feels mortified when he is dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When out' looks like cricket dismissal but signals rearranging E, BATSMAN and FEELS.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-abasement is lowering or degrading oneself, a form of humbling or mortification.

clue.text: Long to have smart clothing? Sewing is required

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping round, so one word dresses the other

parts.note: to smart is to sting
to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: Someone yearns for elegant clothes and is told needlework is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smart' and 'clothing' both suggest fashion, but 'smart' is a verb meaning hurt and 'clothing' means wrapping round.
explanation.definitionFit: Stitching is the work of joining fabric with needle and thread.

clue.text: Approval of choice of commercial?

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
an option is a choice

explanation.surface: Seeking sign-off for which TV commercial to run.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoption of a proposal is its formal acceptance or endorsement.

clue.text: Bird, back by river, tucked into fish little bits at a time

indicators.note: by means beside, so one piece is placed next to the other
back says the word bird is read in reverse
tucked into puts the river letter inside the fish

parts.note: sand dabs are small flatfish

explanation.surface: A bird, returning by a river, pushes into some fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives DRIB; 'tucked into' gives SANDDRABS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dribs and drabs means in small, scattered amounts over a period, idiomatically.

clue.text: Saliva test involved with lip

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A medical swab test that involves the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Spittle is the watery fluid in the mouth, a plain synonym of spit.

clue.text: One who flies from Scandinavia to Russia

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone who travels by plane between Scandinavia and Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes the letters out of 'Scandinavia to'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviator is a pilot, a person who flies aircraft.

clue.text: Posh folk gradually changing sides

indicators.note: changing sides means left is swapped for right

parts.note: gently means gradually

explanation.surface: Upper-class people slowly switching political allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: L (left) becomes R (right), signalled by 'changing sides'.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are the class of well-born people just below the nobility.

clue.text: He scored 100 batting in international trophy, making comeback

indicators.note: in places the hundred and batting inside the reversed trophy
making a comeback means the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: a cup is a trophy
C is the Roman numeral for 100
a cricket batsman who is batting is in

explanation.surface: A cricketer hit a century while playing in a cup match, helping his side fight back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making comeback' gives PUCI, and 'in' splits it after its third letter. 'He scored' means composed music, not runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Puccini composed operas such as La Bohème, so he wrote musical scores.

clue.text: Secured by advance payment, I start to make a living

indicators.note: secured by means held within, so the stake goes round the other pieces

parts.note: an ante is a stake paid in advance, as in poker

indicators.note: start to asks for the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone, backed by money paid up front, begins to earn a livelihood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to' gives M from 'make'; 'Secured by' puts I, M and A inside ANTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Animate as an adjective means alive, the opposite of inanimate.

clue.text: Bikini for one adult comes with cost

parts.note: A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult
a toll is a cost or charge

explanation.surface: Swimwear for a grown-up comes with a price tag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bikini' looks like swimwear; it is Bikini Atoll in the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: Bikini is a ring-shaped coral island in the Marshall Islands, an example of the type.

clue.text: Expression tense for Mike and Wally

indicators.note: tense for Mike means one letter replaces the other

parts.note: an idiom is an expression
Mike is the radio alphabet word for M
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A phrase that is strained on behalf of two friends called Mike and Wally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wally' looks like a man's name beside Mike; it is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Wally is British slang for a silly person, a synonym of idiot.

clue.text: Cast get a car to Petersham?

indicators.note: cast means thrown about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to the cast to drive to Petersham, a place near Richmond in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Petersham reads as the London district but is a heavy overcoat named after Lord Petersham; the question mark flags an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A petersham was a heavy overcoat, so it is an example of this long winter coat.

clue.text: Rev returned to fetch something small and valuable

indicators.note: returned says the word is written backwards

parts.note: to rev an engine is to gun it
to fetch is to get

explanation.surface: A clergyman comes back to collect a small treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rev' suggests a vicar; it is the engine verb, GUN, which 'returned' turns into NUG.
explanation.definitionFit: A nugget is a lump of gold, or figuratively a small valuable piece of information.

clue.text: Knowing about April being stormy as spring proceeds?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: sly means knowing or cunning

indicators.note: stormy means turbulent, so the month's letters are churned

explanation.surface: Wise about April's showers as the season advances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being stormy' gives PIRAL and 'about' wraps it. 'spring' is a coil, not the season.
explanation.definitionFit: A coiled metal spring winds in a helix, so it proceeds in a spiral manner.
